events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
This file is a safety dispute filed by the rider, and the chat record contains a driver message tagged as a threat. At 17:19 the rider asked to stop and get out [F3]; one minute later, at 17:20, the driver wrote "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4], and the system's keyword tagging flagged that message for "lock the door" [F5]. Under RD-... SAFE-1, threat/intimidation language in the chat record requires that no automatic ruling be made and that the matter go to a human reviewer [F4][F5][SAFE-1].

The rider's factual account is otherwise unremarkable on the numbers: the trip ran 15.4 km against a 15.5 km optimal route (-0.1 km) [F1] and 23.2 min against a 22 min estimate (+1.4 min) [F2]. Those records describe the whole ride, not the interval between 17:19 and drop-off, so they neither confirm nor disprove what happened inside the car; the flat RydeX fare of $32.86 was quoted up front and the distance record shows no excess to refund [F1][FARE-1].

What is disputed is exactly what a human reviewer must resolve: whether the physical acts alleged (doors locked, refusal to stop) occurred, versus the driver's contemporaneous statement that the rider tried to open the door while the vehicle was moving and he told her to sit down for her own safety [F6]. There is no GPS, telematics or third-party corroboration of either version; both chat messages are the only record [F3][F4][F5]. Facts to check: the in-car timeline and vehicle telematics/door-lock and stop data around 17:19–17:21, whether the vehicle stopped after the 17:19 request, and any audio/video the driver may hold. A rider safety report of this kind should also be handled with the standard escalation routes for injury/dangerous-conduct allegations [SAFE-2].

Neither party's profile carries this case: the rider shows 709 days, 4.8 rating, 0 disputes in 90 days [F7], and the driver 510 days, 4.66 rating, 786 trips, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days [F8], so no repeated-conduct account action arises on this file [F7][F8][RD-6].

claims.assertion: The in-app chat shows the rider asking to be let out at 17:19 and the driver answering one minute later with a threat to lock her in the car — a threat/intimidation message recorded verbatim in the chat log.
The threat classification is corroborated by the system's own keyword tagging of the driver's message #2 at 17:20 for the phrase 'lock the door', so this is not merely the rider's characterisation.

SAFE-1 applies to threats in the chat record and requires that no automatic ruling be made: the case must be escalated to human review with a factual summary, which is the only correct disposition here.

The rider's account is consistent with the rest of the record: the trip ran 23.2 min against a 22 min estimate and covered 15.4 km of the 15.5 km optimal route, so there is no route or fare irregularity to explain away the mid-trip stop request and the driver's refusal.

This incident is out of character for both accounts — the rider (709 days, 4.8 rating, 0 disputes in 90 days) and the driver (510 days, 4.66 rating, 786 trips, 0 upheld disputes) — so the escalation should be treated as a factual safety report for human assessment rather than as a pattern of abuse.

The driver's written statement admits he told the rider to sit down while the car was moving; even on his own account he used his authority over the doors and the moving vehicle after the rider asked to leave, which the human reviewer should weigh.

weaknesses: The rider has no GPS or timestamp fact showing the doors were actually locked or the car actually stopped/refused to stop; F4 is chat content only, so the physical act described in the complaint is not independently recorded.

The driver's statement (F6) offers a legitimate-sounding safety justification ('she tried to open the door while we were moving'), and no system record contradicts it, so the reviewer may read the message as a safety instruction rather than a threat.

No safety or incident facts exist for this case beyond the chat keyword tag (F5); there is no independent third-party or telematics corroboration, and the profile facts show no prior pattern on either side (F7, F8), which cuts against any finding of repeated conduct.

claims.assertion: The one message relied on by the rider (F4, 17:20 "Sit down or I lock the doors") is a single safety instruction issued in response to a moving-vehicle situation, as recorded in the driver's own contemporaneous statement F6 that the rider tried to open the door while the car was moving; the rider's first message F3 at 17:19 was a request to stop, not an allegation of threat.
The keyword flag F5 is a data-layer keyword match on the words "lock the door" and adds no fact beyond F4; it is not independent evidence of a threat, intimidation or harassment under SAFE-1.

The GPS record F1 shows the trip was completed on the optimal route (15.4 km actual vs 15.5 km optimal, -0.1 km) and F2 shows a duration of 23.2 min vs 22 min estimated, so the ride itself was neither prolonged nor diverted and nothing in the trip record shows the vehicle being stopped against the rider's will.
The fixed RydeX fare of $32.86 was quoted up front and GPS F1 shows no excess distance, so there is no overcharge element for the court to refund.

The driver's account shows 786 trips in the last 90 days with 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes in 90 days (F8), and the rider also has 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F7), so there is no record of repeated violations by either party and no basis for account action.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint is corroborated by a system-recorded chat message at 17:20 containing a detected threat keyword (F4, F5) - the words "I lock the doors" are on the record in the driver's own message, so the threat wording itself cannot be denied and SAFE-1 may well require escalation on that record alone.

The driver's justification is only his own statement (F6), which under the rules loses to system records; there is no GPS or video fact confirming that the rider actually opened or attempted to open the moving door, and no fact showing when the vehicle next stopped after 17:19.
F2 shows the ride took 1.4 min longer than estimated, which the rider could use to argue the driver did not promptly stop after the 17:19 request, though it is within normal variation.

points.response: The riding advocate's own brief concedes the wording 'I lock the doors' is on the record in the driver's own message; F4 is not neutralised by the later self-serving explanation F6, and F3 shows the rider had asked to get out one minute earlier, which is precisely the situation SAFE-1 covers (threat/intimidation in the chat record) rather than a finding this court must adjudicate itself.

Conceded: F5 is a keyword tag derived from F4 and adds no independent fact, so my C2 should not be read as separate corroboration — SAFE-1's escalation trigger is met by F4 itself, which is a system-recorded chat fact.

The driver's point cuts against him: F1 and F2 describe the whole 15.4 km trip, not the events between 17:19 and drop-off, so they cannot show that the vehicle was ever stopped for the rider after her F3 request; escalation under SAFE-1 is required by the threat wording in F4, not by route or duration data.

Conceded, and it is irrelevant to my request: I never sought a refund of the flat RydeX fare, and my only requested outcome is escalate for the threat in F4 — the absence of excess distance in F1 does not answer a safety escalation under SAFE-1.
Conceded on this record: F7 and F8 show zero disputes and zero upheld disputes on both accounts, so I do not ask for any account flag against the driver and withdraw no claim resting on RD-6.

The one minute gap between the rider's stop request (F3, 17:19) and the driver's message (F4, 17:20) is consistent with a driver reacting to an immediate in-car safety situation, not with a premeditated threat, and F6 records that the rider tried to open the door while the vehicle was moving - so the words in F4 are a safety instruction about the door, not intimidation directed at the rider.

F5 is merely the system's keyword tag of the same words in F4 ("lock the door"), so it duplicates rather than corroborates the message and supplies no independent evidence of threat or intimidation under SAFE-1.

Conceded: my client does not contest that a verbatim driver chat message with a detected threat keyword is on the record (F4, F5), and SAFE-1 admits of no automatic ruling on such content, so escalation to human review is the appropriate disposition - which is also what I request.

C4 supports my client rather than the rider: F1 shows the trip was completed on the optimal route (15.4 km vs 15.5 km, -0.1 km) and F2 shows only a 1.4 min variation, so the trip record shows no refusal to stop, no delay attributable to the driver and no irregularity the court could act on.

I agree the record shows no pattern on either side - F8 records 786 trips with 0 upheld disputes for the driver and F7 records 0 disputes for the rider - so no account flag or sanction should attach to my client from this single incident.

F6 is the driver's own statement and is the only source for what physically happened; it contains no admission of a threat, and F1/F2 show the ride continued normally on the optimal route to Bedok Mall, so the message in F4 is best read as a direction to remain seated in a moving vehicle.

I withdraw any suggestion that the trip record disproves a safety event; F1 and F2 establish only that the route and duration were normal and cannot speak to what happened inside the vehicle, so they are neutral as between the parties.
